item.description:
### Added - **Tenant Readiness › API access:** checks which products the API client can use and whether its role in ZIA, Private Access and Client Connector allows what the app writes, naming any missing or read-only permission and where to fix it. - **Tenant Readiness › Prerequisites:** the core ZIA features every POV shows (URL Filtering, Cloud App Control, File Type Control, Advanced Threat Protection, Cloud Firewall, DNS Security, SSL Inspection, malware protection) are checked right after API access; one that isn't licensed is shown in red with the subscription to add to the trial. Home and the summary report list them too. - **Licence editions:** readiness, Customize and the summary report now say which editions the tenant has (Cloud Firewall Standard or Advanced, DNS tunnel detection, Sandbox Standard or Advanced, Data Protection, Browser Isolation), and readiness shows its ZDX tier. - **Licences on this tenant:** the full list of the tenant's subscriptions, with what each one is and unlocks, saved as CSV or opened to print. - **Cloud Firewall Standard:** on a tenant with the standard Cloud Firewall, the geo-blocking rules now match by port (SSH, FTP, Telnet, SMB and an RDP service the app creates) and the QUIC rule by its service; the application-based firewall rules and DNS tunnel detection, which need Advanced Cloud Firewall, are left out and listed. Pick the edition on Customize. - **ZPA Manage, ordered delete:** see what uses each object, preview the delete, and delete in the order ZPA needs. Anything still used by an object you didn't pick is held back (Select It Too picks it), and an App Connector Group waits until each provisioning key ZPA would delete with it is picked too; a segment leaves the wizard's segment group first; ZPA is read again before deleting and nothing is deleted if a picked object changed, and a failed delete skips what depended on it. - **Policy Simulator, multiple rules match:** a result now lists the later rules that also match the traffic. The first one decides, so they don't apply, but they show overlapping or shadowed policy; any that would act differently is marked, and catch-all and default rules are counted. Covered: URL Filtering, Firewall, DNS Control, SSL Inspection, Cloud App Control, Sandbox, File Type Control, Private Access access policy and Cloud & Branch Connector forwarding. Every module shows each one's list, and Bulk Test's CSV has an Also matched column. - **Prove it, for every kind of web test:** URL filtering, threat protection (EICAR and AMTSO), a cloud app, the firewall (destination, port and protocol) and DNS (including DNS over HTTPS), checked the way the Policy Simulator does it, with a Prove It button on each runbook test and the last hour's threat and firewall totals from Z-Insights. On POV Tests and each Active POV's page. - **POV test kit:** POV Tests now offers only what the POV covers: DLP test data for its market (healthcare, financial services, education, public sector or generic personal data), with valid check digits on provider, DEA, routing and card numbers; links to the EICAR and AMTSO malware test pages; and a harmless PDF for Cloud Sandbox, new every time, that says what the POV's Sandbox rules will do with it. - **AI Guard:** a new ZIA page (and a POV Start product) that sends the AI apps through ZIA inspection to AI Guard, following Zscaler's integration guide: it uploads the AI Guard CA, creates the proxy, destination group, QUIC block, an SSL Inspect rule above Microsoft 365's bypass and the forwarding rule (the proxy gateway is one step in the ZIA portal), allows the sanctioned AI apps in ZIA, and sets a compliance profile in AI Guard (HIPAA, HITRUST, PCI DSS, GDPR, CJIS, FERPA, SOX, NIST 800-171, NIST 800-53 or General; Monitor or Block). Prompt capture is opt-in. Dry run first, Apply after review, Undo after; the certificate file is never saved. - **Several tenants at once:** on a POV's page, add its tenant's API key and switch to it while the tenant you were in stays signed in. Those keys are kept in memory only, never saved, and are forgotten after 12 hours unused. Opening a POV switches to its tenant when its key is held; Connect lists the keys held, and Disconnect signs out of the current tenant only. - **ZDX licence tiers:** the ZDX tier comes from the tenant's subscriptions (or pick it); templates and apps the tier doesn't include are marked Not Licensed, and a new ZDX Standard POV template fits ZDX Standard.
### Changed - **ZTH Ebook:** a caution page for AI and ML sites is back, now on the AI and ML category. - **Cloud Sandbox licence:** Advanced now needs the Sandbox Advanced subscription; Advanced Threat Protection brings Standard. Tenants with Sandbox Standard or Advanced Threat Protection but not Sandbox Advanced now start on the Standard rules (you can still pick Advanced on Customize). - **Customize:** a policy module the tenant isn't licensed for now starts switched off, with a note; switch it back on to include it anyway. - **Policy Simulator, workloads:** a Cloud or Branch Connector rule that drops the traffic is now always the result, even if a rule above it might match instead; the connector's conditions are listed when Private Access decides or the connector bypasses Zscaler, and a connector rule that sends traffic direct reads as a bypass. - **DLP test data:** the sample ICD-10 code `I10.0`, which isn't a valid code, is now `I10`; the magnetic-stripe samples are gone.
### Fixed - Readiness no longer flags an SSL Inspect rule limited to destination IP groups as one that inspects everything.
